Class ScreenMatcher

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ScreenMatcher
public final class ScreenMatcher extends Object
Which screens a registered slot (or any feature meant for every inventory screen) applies to. Features are on everywhere by default, and opted out per screen.

The default, all(), is every AbstractContainerScreen: you register once and the feature appears on every screen it could. Naming screens narrows that on purpose. It avoids the old trap where .on(InventoryScreen) quietly missed creative, which is a sibling class, not a subclass:

  • all(), every container screen (the default).
  • allExcept(Class...), every container screen but the named ones (a deliberate exclusion, e.g. "not in creative").
  • only(Class...), only the named screens (full narrowing).
  • where(Predicate), the screens a test accepts, asked of the open screen itself (7.3.0): for a scope only known per menu at runtime, such as "the menus a slot group's slots were added to".

Matching is by class ancestry, the same isAssignableFrom test ScreenPanelAdapter.matches(AbstractContainerScreen) uses, so naming a base class matches its subclasses.

Immutable; one instance can be shared freely.

    • where

      public static ScreenMatcher where(Predicate<? super net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?>> test)
      The screens test accepts, asked of each container screen as it opens (its init, when its menu already holds every slot). For a scope that is not a set of screen classes: a slot library's group, say, whose slots the server adds to some menus and not others, so a panel showing them belongs on exactly those screens (adapter.onMatching(group.screens())). It is decided when the screen opens and not asked again while it stays open: a creative tab switch, which swaps the menu's slots on the same screen, doesn't ask it again. What changes while the screen is open is the panel's mode scope (Panel.Builder.in(ModeScope, Placement)) or its visibleWhen, not this. The test runs on the render thread; it must not throw.

    • matches

      public boolean matches(Class<?> screenClass)
      Whether this matcher applies to an open screen's class. The mixins already check for AbstractContainerScreen, so all() always matches. A where(Predicate) matcher has no answer from the class alone and says yes; ask matches(AbstractContainerScreen).
